title: Decentralized health-prober and quorum rollback for VPC runtime switchover
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Improve private (VPC) data-plane runtime switchover reliability by implementing a decentralized health prober that produces a quorum-based rollout decision and an automated rollback path that preserves KV cache and in-flight request safety. This ticket covers the operator + Terraform hooks, a lightweight prober running on each runtime shard, traffic shadowing for warm-up, and an automated rollback safety net when quorum checks fail.
acceptance_criteria: A protobuf-compatible health probe agent runs on every runtime node and reports per-shard readiness with explicit priming and cache-warm indicators
The upgrade operator collects prober outputs and makes a quorum decision (>= 75% healthy shards) before shifting live traffic
Traffic is shadowed to new runtime for at least N successful requests or M seconds (configurable) before cutover
Automated rollback triggers if quorum not reached within the configured window or error budget is exceeded, returning all live traffic to the previous runtime within the SLA window
Terraform module exposes flags (enable_quorum_gating, shadow_duration_sec, quorum_threshold) and outputs the runtime_switch_id for audits
End-to-end integration tests validate rollback recovers cache state or gracefully drains without request loss in >95% test runs
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Build a minimal health-prober sidecar binary that exposes /probe with JSON status: {uptime, avg_latency_ms, primed_kv_fraction, last_error} (stateless, <2MB)
Phase 2: Extend runtime k8s operator to aggregate probes via CRD (RuntimeHealthStatus) and compute quorum at the tenant level
Phase 3: Add Terraform outputs and a module option to flip runtime_switch_id; add a preflight data-plane check step in the Terraform apply pipeline
Phase 4: Implement shadowing middleware in the routing tier to send a configurable percentage of requests and priming workloads to the target runtime during warm-up
Phase 5: Wire automated rollback: operator watches for quorum failure/timeouts and triggers controlled traffic reversion + cache reconciliation hooks
Phase 6: Add telemetry dashboards and alerting (quorum failures, warm-up latency, priming success rate) to Console and PagerDuty integrations
rollout_plan: Canary: Select 5 low-traffic tenants and perform end-to-end upgrade with shadowing enabled and quorum threshold set to 100% for strict validation
Small ramp: 25% tenant cohort with quorum_threshold=85% and shadow_duration_sec=300
Wide roll: 100% but with dynamic quorum_threshold=default (75%) and staggered tenant windows to avoid blast radius
Rollback conditions: any sustained increase in 5xx > 1.5x baseline for 5 minutes OR quorum below threshold for the configured window OR primed_kv_fraction < 0.6 after shadowing
Rollback action: operator performs immediate traffic switch to previous runtime version, triggers cache-check job, and creates a runbook incident with automated diagnostics attached
test_plan: Unit tests for prober binary validating JSON schema and edge states (disk full, slow responses)
Integration test harness that deploys two runtime versions in a test VPC, exercises shadowed traffic, simulates shard failures, and asserts quorum-driven behavior
Chaos tests: kubelet kill, network partitions, and delayed KV priming to verify rollback triggers and recovery flow
Load test: ensure shadowing at 10% of production QPS does not increase p99 > baseline + 10%
End-to-end runbook dry-run where Ops follows automated rollback and validates telemetry artifacts and audit logs
migration_steps: Add prober sidecar to runtime Helm chart and a feature flag to enable per-tenant probing
Upgrade operator image and CRD versions in staging and run smoke tests
Expose Terraform variables for gating config and apply to staging with 'enable_quorum_gating=true'
Run canary upgrades for 5 tenants, collect telemetry for 48h, and adjust thresholds if needed
Promote changes to production Terraform with a staged apply and manual approval step for the first wide roll
notes: We intentionally choose a decentralized prober to avoid single-point-of-failure in the control plane — each shard reports independently and the operator only observes the aggregated state.
Priming indicator (primed_kv_fraction) helps avoid post-cutover latency spikes due to cold KV caches; we will instrument KV shrink/growth to refine thresholds.
Terraform coupling: we make the switch controlled by a runtime_switch_id that is output from TF and annotated in the operator event stream for traceability.
Security: prober endpoints will be restricted to the control-plane network and authenticated via mTLS using existing service-cert rotation.
Cost note: shadowing increases egress and compute for the warm-up window; default shadow_duration_sec=300 is conservative but should be tuned per tenant size.
